paper.citation: Camgoz, Koller, Hadfield, and Bowden. 2020. Sign Language Transformers: Joint End-to-End Sign Language Recognition and Translation. CVPR.

code_artifacts.role: Published training, development selection, and test implementation

datasets.name: RWTH-PHOENIX-Weather 2014T
datasets.version_or_subset: PHOENIX14T train/dev/test with pami0 1024-D pretrained CNN frame features
datasets.license_or_permission: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; non-commercial research and project-cloud processing
datasets.deviation: The authors' feature URLs no longer resolve. A pinned public mirror was used, and its protocol-5 declaration was changed to protocol 4 while preserving all subsequent decompressed bytes. Cryptographic equivalence to the unavailable author-hosted files cannot be established.

guesses: The direct request to reproduce repositories/neccam/slt was resolved to the repository's supplied default joint lambda_R=1, lambda_T=1 configuration and its matching Table 4 row.
The paper does not identify the seed or score aggregation behind Table 4; the published configuration pins seed 42, so one seed-42 run was used.
deviations: The unavailable author-hosted pami0 archives were replaced by a checksum-pinned public mirror whose identity with the originals cannot be proven.
The mirror's pickle protocol declaration was changed from 5 to 4 for Python 3.7; every later decompressed byte is identical.
PyTorch/torchvision/torchtext 1.4.0/0.5.0/0.5.0 were replaced by 1.7.1+cu110/0.8.2+cu110/0.8.1 so the A100 could execute; one integer-division compatibility patch restores the old beam-index dtype.
The supplied config searches recognition and translation beams 1 through 10 and translation alphas -1 through 5, while the paper states beams 0 through 10 and alphas 0 through 2.
The supplied config uses learning_rate_min=1e-7, while the paper states 1e-6.
The paper does not report A100 hardware or the exact CUDA stack used here.
